messages.author: ab78e227e394cf1d
messages.subject: Hyperparameter in f(ID,model="iid")
parts:
Hi INLA Authors,

I have a question related to the precision hyperparameter for iid model. 

In the output of INLA

Link: https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-mixed.html#independent-random-effects-iid-model:~:text=3.3.1%20Independent%20random-,effects,-(iid%20model)

Precision for ID = 7 :=\tau

does it mean as   ID \sim N(0, \frac{1/tau}) or else,

ID \sim N(0,\tau)?

My understanding is the first choice as a conclusion is written there as a better choice of model with higher precision. 

Thank you in advance!

Alokesh.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hyperparameter in f(ID,model="iid")
parts:
Hi Dr. Rue,

I want a bit more clarity.

Say for IID it is written that

"The precision matrix of iid random effects is 
τΣ with Σ a diagonal matrix of scaling factors {s1,…,sn}
 (which are all equal to 1 by default). Scaling factors are defined by means of parameter scale within the f() function used to define the latent effect in the formula."

So when we obtain Precision for ID

are we obtaining 1/τ or τ?

Alokesh.
